all_violations.description: The otherwise-valid expired/future proof fixture derives issuance and five-minute expiry from live Node Date.now(), then submits the HMAC proof to a real database clock. No fake or injected clock governs this fixture; proof validity depends on the relation between the runner clock, DB clock and elapsed scheduling time. This meets H2 even though the offsets provide a useful practical margin.
all_violations.suggestion: Derive mutated timestamps from the prepared DB challenge issuance rather than the independent Node wall clock; retain explicit expired/future cases and fixed-clock unit boundary assertions. Do not fake an unauthenticated success response or weaken the DB-time check.
all_violations.code_snippet: const issued = Date.now() + (state === "expired" ? -600_000 : 120_000);
all_violations.predicate_evidence: p_attestation_issued_at and p_attestation_expires_at are time-bounded authorization values created from live clock with no fake timers. new Date at line269 formats the derived timestamps.

all_violations.description: The synthetic proof gets only three seconds remaining from live PostgreSQL clock_timestamp(), before asynchronous contact-lock acquisition, second-session startup and pg_blocking_pids polling. An otherwise correct implementation fails the beforeExpiry.fresh assertion at line174 if that setup is scheduled after the three-second boundary. Later observed-expiry polling proves a real post-lock boundary, but does not freeze or remove this live-clock freshness race.
all_violations.suggestion: Retain the actual PostgreSQL clock_timestamp expiry semantics, transaction lock barrier and no-audit assertions. Make the near-expiry setup budget explicit and validate freshness before admitting the asserted race; derive timestamps consistently from one DB clock sample. Do not freeze Node timers as DB control or add an unapproved production clock seam. Fixed-clock pure proof boundaries remain separate evidence.
all_violations.code_snippet: const [times] = await holder.query<{ issued: string; expires: string }>("select public.file_signed_access_attestation_iso(clock_timestamp()-interval '4 minutes 57 seconds') as issued,public.file_signed_access_attestation_iso(clock_timestamp()+interval '3 seconds') as expires");
all_violations.predicate_evidence: Live DB clock constructs a security-relevant five-minute proof lifetime with three seconds remaining and no fake clock. This is an H2 fixture, not H1: the while loop polls DB expiration rather than sleeping.
